messages:
Zoe: Hey y'all, Zoe here (first day!). On an M3 Mac with macOS Ventura. Trying to follow the dotfiles bootstrap to get asdf managing python 3.11, node 18, and rust. Python and node mostly ok after brew deps, but cargo build for a repo crate fails with `openssl-sys`/`ring` errors: header not found. Also noticed the rust plugin for asdf installs rustup under the hood. Should I use asdf or rustup directly?

rachel: welcome Zoe! :tada: We standardize on asdf so .tool-versions in repos work everywhere. asdf-rust delegates to rustup toolchains, so it's effectively rustup but managed by asdf. For the openssl errors on M-series, make sure brew is ARM at /opt/homebrew and install the right libs: `brew install openssl@3 pkg-config cmake` (openssl@3 preferred for modern crates).

ben: +1. Then export env vars so cargo/cbindgen find them: `export OPENSSL_DIR="$(brew --prefix openssl@3)"` and `export PKG_CONFIG_PATH="$OPENSSL_DIR/lib/pkgconfig"`. For some crates also `export OPENSSL_LIB_DIR="$OPENSSL_DIR/lib"` and `export OPENSSL_INCLUDE_DIR="$OPENSSL_DIR/include"`. Put those in `~/.shell_env` (dotfiles bootstrap can write this).

Zoe: cool. Is there any reason to install openssl@1.1 too? Some Python builds earlier mentioned 1.1 in docs.

rachel: historically python builds referenced openssl@1.1, but on recent macOS and newer Python versions openssl@3 usually works. For Python 3.11 if you see missing headers, point the build to brew's openssl similarly with CPPFLAGS/LDFLAGS, e.g.: `export LDFLAGS="-L$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/lib"` `export CPPFLAGS="-I$(brew --prefix openssl@3)/include"`. If a repo explicitly pins openssl@1.1 we'll note it in that repo's README.

Zoe: got it. About rustup vs asdf: any issues with cargo getting installed twice or PATH order?

ben: ensure `~/.asdf/shims` is earlier in PATH than any /usr/local/bin rustup-managed `cargo`. After bootstrap, open a new login shell. `asdf which cargo` should point into `~/.asdf/installs/rust/.../bin/cargo`. If you previously used rustup directly and have `~/.cargo/bin` in PATH, move asdf shims first or remove the old `~/.cargo/bin` entry.

devex: note: dotfiles bootstrap warns about existing rust installs and offers to back up `~/.cargo`. It will also add `export PATH="$HOME/.asdf/shims:$HOME/.asdf/bin:$PATH"` to your shell env.

Zoe: Node question: when adding nodejs plugin it asked me to import GPG keys and then errored with pinentry. Same as others?

rachel: yeah run `brew install gpg pinentry-mac` then `export GPG_TTY=$(tty)` and `bash ~/.asdf/plugins/nodejs/bin/import-release-team-keyring`. If pinentry prompts weirdly, `gpgconf --kill gpg-agent && gpgconf --launch gpg-agent` usually helps. You can also set `ASDF_NODEJS_USE_DIST=1` to skip compile for onboarding if you're blocked.

Zoe: 1Password CLI flow for loading dev secrets into .envrc — anything org-specific?

devex: install `op` via brew, then `op signin` and use the dotfiles helper `scripts/load-secrets.sh` which will populate `.env.local`. We recommend storing per-project keys in 1Password and never committing .env.local. Dotfiles include a `direnv` hook that reads `.env.local` if present.

Zoe: SSH/GitHub access: I added my pubkey to GitHub. How long until I can push to private repos?

infra-bot: created onboarding ticket ONB-1001 for Zoe. Infra runs key sync every 20 minutes; once your public key is visible infra will grant org repo access automatically. If you need immediate access DM @rachel for escalation.

ben: last tip: M3-specific quirk  if you ever hit weird linker errors, run `arch -arm64 zsh -l` to ensure a clean ARM login shell so brew paths resolve correctly. Also run `brew doctor` if things look off.

Zoe: perfect, thanks everyone! I'll add the OPENSSL_DIR exports to ~/.shell_env and re-run cargo install. Appreciate the quick help :heart:
